intro: Hindu texts are full of stories. They are also full of big ideas about how to live. In this unit you will learn four of those ideas: dharma, karma, samsara and moksha. You will see how Hindu families connect them to stories you already know.

Then you will follow a year of Hindu festivals, from Pongal in January to Diwali in the fall. You will learn what happens in puja at home and in a temple. You will also visit, in words, the Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago in Lemont, Illinois.
By the end, you will be able to explain each key idea in your own words. You will name the stories festivals remember. You will also know how to be a respectful guest at a place of worship.
bigQuestion: How do Hindu ideas and festivals help families live out the stories of their texts?

timeline.t: Pongal and Makar Sankranti give thanks for the harvest and the sun
Maha Shivaratri: many Hindus honor Shiva with a night of prayer
Holi: bonfires remember Prahlad, and colors fill the streets
Rama Navami celebrates the birth of Rama
Janmashtami celebrates the birth of Krishna at midnight
Ganesh Chaturthi honors Ganesha, the remover of obstacles
Navaratri and Durga Puja honor the Goddess for nine nights
Dussehra remembers Rama's victory over Ravana
Diwali, the festival of lights, welcomes Rama home and honors Lakshmi

words.d: duty, what is right, and the right way to live
action; Hindus believe every action has results
the cycle of birth, death and rebirth many Hindus believe in
freedom or release; many Hindus believe it is freedom from rebirth
the one ultimate reality many Hindus believe is behind everything
Hindu worship with offerings such as flowers, light and food
food offered in worship and then shared as a blessing
a sacred image of a deity, honored in temples and homes
seeing and being seen by the deity
the Hindu festival of lights in October or November
a calendar that follows both the moon and the sun

test.q: Which word means duty and the right way to live?
test.why: Dharma means duty and what is right.

test.q: What do Hindus believe about karma?
test.why: Karma means action, and Hindus believe actions have results.

test.q: Many Hindus believe moksha is freedom from what?
test.why: Many Hindus believe moksha is freedom from samsara.

test.q: Which Gita verse tells Arjuna to work without greed for reward?
test.why: Bhagavad Gita 2.47 is the famous verse about the right to work, not its results.

test.q: What does the Rig Veda verse 1.164.46 say about the One?
test.why: Rig Veda 1.164.46 says the wise call the One by many names.

test.q: Which is one of the four aims of life?
test.why: Kama, enjoyment, is one of the four aims.

test.q: Which path in the Gita is loving devotion?
test.why: Bhakti is the path of loving devotion.

test.q: Who honors Vishnu as the Supreme?
test.why: Vaishnavas honor Vishnu, often as Rama or Krishna.

test.q: Which festival welcomes Rama home with lamps?
test.why: Many Hindus say Diwali lamps welcome Rama home.
The Devi Mahatmya tells how Durga defeats Mahishasura.

choices: Waving a lamp before a murti
test.why: Arati is worship in which a lamp is waved before a murti.

test.q: Where is the Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago?
test.why: The Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago is in Lemont, Illinois.

test.q: Why do many Hindu calendars add an extra month?
choices: To stay in step with the seasons
test.why: Twelve moon months are shorter than a sun year, so an extra month keeps the seasons in line.

test.q: What should a guest do at a Hindu temple?
choices: Take off shoes and speak quietly
test.why: Guests show respect by taking off shoes and keeping quiet voices.

write.prompt: Pick one Hindu festival from this unit. Explain what story it remembers and which idea it connects to (dharma, karma or bhakti). Cite the text, such as the Ramayana or the Bhagavata Purana, and one Gita verse if it fits.
tips: Name the text you are using, like Ramayana or Bhagavata Purana.
Say "many Hindus believe" when you share a belief.
Use at least two words from the unit, like puja, prasad or dharma.
Describe what families do; do not judge it.
